title: Serve the assignment ledger as one server row: stage, submissions, stall
acceptance: Store: workspace W has 60 lifecycles and case C whose lifecycle is the 60th-newest with stage 'collecting' -> listCaseLedger(50, W) returns C with stage 'collecting' (today the table's caseStage falls back to 'published'/'approved' because GET /api/devcase/lifecycle only carries the 50 newest lifecycles)
Store: case with no lifecycle and one open posting -> stage 'published'; with no lifecycle and no posting -> stage 'approved' (the caseStage fallback preserved, now computed in SQL)
Store: case with two postings carrying 2 and 3 submissions -> submissionCount 5; lifecycleUpdatedAt and lifecycleCreatedAt present so stallForCase gets the same inputs the table computes today

body:
## Summary
The Assignments ledger computes each row's stage, submission count and stall by joining three separately-bounded client lists (cases up to 500, lifecycles capped at 50, every posting with every submission). Past fifty lifecycles the join silently shows the wrong stage, the stage filter only sees the loaded page, and the table pays for full case JSON and every evaluation bundle to draw a count. Move the join into one store read that returns a ledger projection per case, filtered before the limit, and give the detail reader its own by-id read.

## Description
Add `listCaseLedger(limit, ws, filters)` to app/_lib/db/devcase.ts: dev_cases LEFT JOIN the latest dev_lifecycle per case_id (stage, created_at, updated_at) and a per-case submission COUNT via dev_postings, with the published/approved fallback in SQL and q/stage/seniority applied in WHERE before LIMIT+1. Ensure an index on dev_lifecycle(workspace_id, case_id) in-store (the submissionStore additive-DDL shape). GET /api/devcase returns these projection rows (identity, jobId/jobTitle/jdSlug, stage, submissionCount, lifecycle timestamps) plus `truncated`; a new GET /api/devcase/[id] (requireOperator, workspace-checked) returns the full record for the detail reader. The client drops caseStage/filterCases in favour of a pure URL builder, and the table reads stage and counts from the row. Postings and lifecycles keep loading for the lifecycle strip and the detail's submissions; the ledger simply stops depending on them.

## Flow
1. Store function + ledger/tenancy tests (acceptance 1-4). 2. GET /api/devcase projection + filters, new [id] route, route tests, `npm run api:docs` (5-6). 3. casesPage URL builder, useDevTabData filter state, DevCasesTable reading row fields, DevTabCasesView fetching the detail on open (7-8). 4. Doc update in docs/features/dev-case/README.md.

## Expected impact
A studio past fifty lifecycles stops mislabelling older live assignments (and hiding their stall chip); the stage filter answers for the whole library instead of the loaded page; the ledger payload drops the need/analysis/role/case JSON and the table no longer needs every evaluation bundle to draw a number. The seam also stops the next feature on this table (sort, job filter, counts) from inheriting a three-list client join.

## Evaluation
Claim: the ledger's stage, count and filter are computed once, server-side, over the whole workspace, and are correct past the lifecycle window.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test store/route/URL-builder cases written first, plus the integration gate (tsc, lint, api:check, docs:check, test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract (GET /api/devcase response shape changes; one in-repo consumer).

body:
## Summary
Three surfaces already send people to Assignments with a destination in mind - the Control Room's Art. 22 gate Review link (carries ?lifecycle=), the Job page's 'N assignments' chip, and any future share of a case - and the tab reads none of it: view and selection are local state, the review panel opens only on its own click. Make the tab an address: ?lifecycle= scrolls to the lifecycle and opens its review panel (or says the gate was already decided), ?case= opens the case reader, ?job= filters the ledger to that role.

## Description
A new pure module assignmentsDeepLink.ts parses the three params (with precedence), resolves an intent against the loaded lists into a view/selection/notice/action, and computes the consumed search string. DevTab reads it once per arrival, waits for the relevant list's first load, applies the resolution, raises the page limit when a case may sit past the page, and strips the params via history.replaceState (the ?arm= one-shot shape). LifecycleSection/Row accept a focus id that scrolls the row into view and opens the review panel when the row is awaiting approval. An unresolvable address leaves the reader where they are and shows a named, localized notice (missing, other team, already decided), per the navigation-model rule for arrivals into a standing session. The Cases table gains a job filter (and a clearable chip); JobsLifecycleStrip passes {job}. `case` and `lifecycle` join TAB_SCOPED_PARAM_KEYS.

## Flow
1. Write assignmentsDeepLink.test.ts (acceptance 1-7) and the filter job case. 2. Implement the module + filter. 3. Wire DevTab/DevTabCasesView/LifecycleSection/LifecycleRow (focus + open review), notices in four catalogs under the lock. 4. tabs.ts keys + pin, JobsLifecycleStrip params (acceptance 8). 5. Doc update (dev-case README) and correct the compliance README sentence if wording changes.

## Expected impact
The Control Room's Review becomes a one-click path to the actual human-gate panel the compliance doc says it is, instead of a list the reviewer must search; a job's assignment chip lands on that job's assignments; a stale gate link explains itself instead of silently showing a table. Assignments becomes linkable from the palette, tasks and future notifications with no further work.

## Evaluation
Claim: every address that points into Assignments lands on what it names, or says why it cannot.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over assignmentsDeepLink.ts, DevCasesTable.filter.ts and tabs.ts written first; optional Playwright check that /?tab=assignments&lifecycle=<id> shows the review panel.
Result: pending build.
Gate: none.
